identity.title: An ultra-multiplex CRISPR/Cas9 system for simultaneous editing of 29 genes reshapes the nutritional profile of soybean.

content.abstract: Simultaneous editing of dozens of genes has been a long-standing goal in plant biotechnology. However, this approach faces major technical hurdles, including reduced editing efficiency with increasing numbers of sgRNAs, vector instability caused by repetitive Pol III promoters, and limited capacity of single-transcript-unit systems. These challenges collectively hinder the engineering of complex traits. Soybean is a vital source of plant protein and oil, but anti-nutritional factors and unpleasant flavors degrade its seed quality, and conventional breeding fails to pyramid favorable alleles to eliminate undesirable ones. To resolve these bottlenecks, we developed the Multiple SgRNA Array (MSA) system, a modular and scalable architecture for expanded sgRNA loading while maintaining cloning flexibility and high editing efficiency. Hairy-root assays validated its capacity to edit 46 targets via 32 sgRNAs simultaneously. We deployed MSA in stable soybean transformation to knock out 29 genes across three functional modules: anti-nutritional-factor reduction, flavor refinement, and nodulation optimization. Multi-generation screening generated the rnp-29m mutant with loss-of-function mutations in all 29 genes. This mutant shows enhanced seed traits, elevated oleic acid, decreased allergens and anti-nutrients, improved digestibility, and attenuated beany flavor, with no significant yield penalty. Our modular MSA system enables high-capacity sgRNA assembly and ultra-multiplex editing, providing a robust tool for rapid trait pyramiding and elite soybean germplasm with superior nutrition.
